title: Straightening affine-line-generated smooth subgroups of vector groups
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, with $p$ prime [def-weil-field]. All groups are affine $k$-group schemes of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], and smoothness and connectedness have the meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Write $\mathbf G_a(R)=(R,+)$ [def-sc-gm-ga] and $\mathbb A^1_k=\operatorname{Spec}k[x]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-polynomial-ring]. A vector group means a $k$-group isomorphic to $\mathbf G_a^n$ for some integer $n\geq0$. Let $E=\mathbf G_a^N$ with $N\geq0$, and let $L\subseteq E$ be smooth. Fix a separable closure $K/k$. Suppose $L_K$ is the smallest closed subgroup scheme of $E_K$ through which all members of some set of pointed $K$-scheme morphisms $\mathbb A^1_K\to L_K\hookrightarrow E_K$ factor, where pointed means $0\mapsto0$. Then there exist a $k$-group automorphism $h:E\xrightarrow{\sim}E$ and an integer $0\leq d\leq N$ such that $h(L)=\mathbf G_a^d\times\{0\}^{N-d}$ as closed subgroup schemes of $E$. In particular $L\simeq\mathbf G_a^d$ and there is a $k$-group homomorphism $r:E\to L$ whose restriction to $L$ is the identity. The automorphism is a group-scheme automorphism and is not required to be $k$-linear for the displayed coordinates.

source.place: Proposition 1.15, printed p.9, including the coordinate-automorphism conclusion; the retraction is its coordinate projection. Read online at https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/appbnew.pdf; WANTED locally. No Stacks tag is claimed for this algebraic-group result.

proof.text: Prove the coordinate-subgroup assertion by strong induction on $N$, for every smooth closed subgroup and every generating family in the statement; the isomorphism and retraction will follow in Step 7. For $N=0$ there is only the trivial subgroup. For $N=1$, if $L\ne E$, its defining ideal contains a nonzero polynomial $q\in k[x]$. For every member $u$ of the family, its coordinate is $v(t)\in K[t]$ with $q(v(t))=0$. If $v$ were nonconstant, the leading term of this composition would have degree $\deg(q)\deg(v)$ with nonzero coefficient, a contradiction. Hence $v$ is constant and pointedness makes it zero. Minimality gives $L_K=0$, and then $L=0$: equality of defining ideals is detected by tensoring with $K$, since a $k$-vector space injects into its scalar extension. If $L=E$, use the identity automorphism, in every dimension.

source.place: Proposition 1.15, printed p.9, induction and its n=1 base; degree calculation expanded.

proof.text: Let $N>1$ and $L\ne E$. The polynomial ring $k[x_1,\ldots,x_N]$ is a domain, so its spectrum $E$ is an irreducible affine variety. The polynomial dimension formula gives $\dim E=N$: a field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0,k$) and has dimension zero. A nonzero defining ideal of $L$ has proper vanishing set, since it does not contain the prime $(0)$ in its vanishing set. The affine dimension-drop lemma therefore gives $\dim L\leq N-1$. We treat equality first and strict inequality in Step 6.

source.place: Proposition 1.15, printed p.9, division into codimension one and higher codimension; dimension facts made explicit.

proof.text: If $\dim L=N-1$, the hypersurface equation lemma supplies a $k$-group homomorphism $f:E\to\mathbf G_a$ with scheme-theoretic kernel $L$. Some generating curve in $L_K$ is nonconstant: otherwise every pointed curve in the family is zero, contradicting minimality and $\dim L=N-1>0$. Apply separable axis extraction to $f$ and this curve. It gives $\alpha$ such that $M=\alpha^{-1}(L)$ contains the first coordinate axis $A=\mathbf G_a\times0$. The automorphism is over $k$; no assertion that a vector group admits only linear automorphisms is used.

source.place: Proposition 1.15, printed p.9, codimension-one paragraph, invoking Corollary 1.8 and Lemmas 1.11, 1.13.

proof.text: We record once the projection argument used in both remaining cases. For any smooth closed subgroup $M\subseteq\mathbf G_a\times V'$, $V'=\mathbf G_a^{N-1}$, generated after $K$ by a pointed family, factor $M\to V'$ as a faithfully flat finitely presented quotient $q:M\to I$ followed by a closed immersion $I\hookrightarrow V'$, using the group-homomorphism factorization. Its separatedness hypothesis holds because all groups here are affine. Its kernel is a closed normal subgroup of $M$, and $I$ represents its fppf quotient. The affine normal-quotient lemma gives smoothness of $I$ and identifies $I_K$ with the corresponding quotient over $K$. The projected curves generate $I_K$: if a closed subgroup $J\subseteq V'_K$ contains them, its inverse image in $(\mathbf G_a\times V')_K$ contains $M_K$ by generation. Thus $q_K$ factors through $J\cap I_K$. On coordinate rings the ideal of $J\cap I_K$ pulls back to zero in $\mathcal O(M_K)$; faithful flatness makes this map injective, so the ideal is zero and $I_K\subseteq J$. Finally the image-dimension bound, applied to the surjection $q$, gives $\dim I\leq\dim M$. These statements require neither smoothness nor connectedness of $\ker q$.

source.place: Proposition 1.15, printed p.9, both projections to V prime; quotient and image hypotheses expanded using the existing general group-image lemmas.

proof.text: Continue the codimension-one case with $M$ from Step 3 and $I$ from Step 4. Put $M'=M\cap(0\times V')$. On every $k$-algebra $R$, subtraction of $(a,0)\in A(R)$ from $(a,v)\in M(R)$ shows $(0,v)\in M'(R)$; consequently $M=A\times M'$ as closed subgroup schemes, with inverse maps $(a,v)\mapsto(a,(0,v))$ and addition. The projection $M\to M'$ represents $M/A$ (a section lifts every element and its fibres are exactly the $A$-cosets), so normal-quotient smoothness gives smoothness of $M'$. Its inclusion in $V'$ equals the image $I$: $\mathcal O(M')\to\mathcal O(M')[t]$ is injective, so no additional equation of $V'$ vanishes on $M$. Hence Step 4 gives generation of $M'_K$. Induction on the ambient dimension $N-1$ supplies $\beta\in\operatorname{Aut}_{k\text{-gp}}(V')$ straightening $M'$. Then $(\mathrm{id}\times\beta)\alpha^{-1}$ straightens $L$; permute coordinate axes to put the nonzero factors first.

source.place: Proposition 1.15, printed p.9, equality h prime(U)=V1 times U prime and induction on V prime; the equality is checked on all algebras.

proof.text: If $\dim L<N-1$, apply Step 4 to $M=L$. Induction straightens $I\subseteq V'$ by some $\beta$, since $V'$ has $N-1$ coordinates and $I$ is smooth and generated as required. Write $\beta(I)=\mathbf G_a^e\times0$, moving its nonzero axes first. The polynomial dimension formula gives $e=\dim I\leq\dim L<N-1$, so $e+1<N$. Thus $M=(\mathrm{id}\times\beta)(L)$ is a closed smooth subgroup of the smaller coordinate subgroup $B=\mathbf G_a\times\mathbf G_a^e\times0$. Its transformed curves generate it in $B_K$: every closed subgroup of $B_K$ is also closed in $E_K$, so minimality in $E_K$ applies. Induction in dimension $e+1$ gives a group automorphism of $B$ straightening $M$ there. Extend it by the identity on the remaining $N-e-1$ coordinates, and compose with $\mathrm{id}\times\beta$. This is an automorphism of all of $E$, giving the required coordinate subgroup. Both recursive calls have strictly smaller ambient dimension; even $e=0$ is allowed.

source.place: Proposition 1.15, printed p.9, last paragraph: straighten the projection and induct again in its proper coordinate preimage.

proof.text: Let $h$ be the automorphism obtained above and $C=\mathbf G_a^d\times0=h(L)$ after permuting axes. Restriction $h|_L:L\xrightarrow{\sim}C$ followed by the coordinate identification gives $L\simeq\mathbf G_a^d$. If $P:E\to C$ sets the last $N-d$ coordinates to zero, define $r=(h|_L)^{-1}\circ P\circ h$. Every map is a $k$-group homomorphism, and $P|_C=\mathrm{id}_C$, so $r|_L=\mathrm{id}_L$. This includes $d=0$, $d=N$ and the empty generating family. No connectedness or perfectness assumption has been added.
